fact.claim: From January 1990 to April 2025, when the VIX fear gauge spiked above 40, the S&P 500 was up 30% a year later on average, according to a Wells Fargo Investment Institute analysis. At that average, $10,000 would have become about $13,000. The index was higher 12 months later in more than 90% of these periods, so it did not happen every time. The worst losses followed the 2008 spikes, when stocks kept falling for months. These are past averages and say nothing certain about what comes next.

caption:
Sell in the panic and you can miss the 30% that came after.

From January 1990 to April 2025, when the VIX fear gauge spiked above 40, the S&P 500 was up 30% a year later on average. That's from a Wells Fargo Investment Institute analysis.

At that average, $10,000 held through the panic became about $13,000. Sold that day, it stayed $10,000. That's a $3,000 gap.

It didn't happen every time. The index was higher 12 months later in more than 90% of these periods, and stocks kept falling for months after the 2008 spikes. Past averages aren't a promise about what comes next.

Save this and find your row before the next scary week.

Source: Wells Fargo Investment Institute, via CNBC and NBC New York.
